retail: Customer data: are our safeguards evidence-ready?
South Africa's Information Regulator fined FNB in October for failing to protect customer data. Loyalty and e-commerce data stores carry the same exposure.
When did we last test access controls and breach response on customer data?
AI agents: do we meet the new expectations?
South Africa's regulator co-adopted the Global Privacy Assembly resolution on agentic AI (17 Nov): purpose limits, human oversight and logs.
Which AI assistants or agents are we piloting, and who signs off their data use?
The Competition Commission is applying remedies to X and xAI, and cleared Capitec–Walletdoc with conditions.
Which platform or payment-gateway dependencies would hurt us if their terms change?
fin: POPIA enforcement has reached a major bank
The FNB fine (26 Oct) sets a benchmark that boards will notice.
Can we show the regulator our safeguards today, not just our policies?
Kenya shows where AI-in-banking rules are heading
The Central Bank of Kenya consulted on AI in banking, third-party technology providers and cybersecurity.
Do our models and our technology vendors have evidence of risk controls ready?
Crypto and cross-border rules are tightening
The South African crypto-assets manual consultation has closed, Kenya's VASP licensing is live and Nigeria's rules are in force.
Are our KYC and exchange-control rules updated for each market?
telco: The Electronic Communications Amendment Bill is coming
The consultation closed in August. Access obligations and new regulator powers are the biggest telecoms change in the pipeline.
Which wholesale and network-sharing deals would the access rules change?
A new network deployment policy direction
The Minister's 19 Oct direction sets the approach to rollout and sharing.
Are our fibre and tower plans aligned with it?
Licence transfers (Zoom Fibre, Smile) and Teraco's Cape Town expansion signal new owners and more local cloud.
Which suppliers or partners are changing hands?
all: The FNB fine (26 Oct) is the headline for every sector holding customer data.
Where is our most sensitive customer data, and who can reach it?
The agentic-AI resolution, Kenya's AI-in-banking guidance and the frontier-AI and BRICS commitments all point the same way.
Do we have an inventory of the AI we use, with an owner for each system?
Expanding in Africa now has compliance gates
Egypt's data-protection law is fully enforced, Kenya–EU adequacy talks have concluded, and Nigeria's promotion rules are being updated.
Are regulatory checks built into our cross-border rollout plans?

items.title: Competition Commission concluded voluntary undertaking with X.AI (and settlement with X Corp) replacing Media and Digital Platforms Market Inquiry remedies
items.why: The Commission is applying market-inquiry remedies to AI chatbots and platforms. Brands that rely on platform reach and AI search should expect more rules on how platforms treat local content.

items.title: National Bank of Ethiopia Regulatory Sandbox Directive entered into force
items.why: A regulatory sandbox route is now open for fintech pilots in Ethiopia.

items.title: Global Privacy Assembly (incl. South Africa) adopted Resolution on Privacy-protective Agentic AI
items.why: Data-protection regulators, South Africa's among them, set shared expectations for AI agents. These are a useful yardstick for AI-agent deployments: purpose limits, human oversight, logging.

items.title: Kenya and the European Union concluded their data-protection Adequacy Dialogue
items.why: Could ease data transfers between the EU and Kenya. A useful benchmark for any future South Africa–EU adequacy push.

items.title: Central Bank of Kenya closed consultations on AI in Banking, Third-Party Technology Service Providers and Cybersecurity guidance notes
items.why: The first AI-in-banking guidance in the region, plus rules for technology vendors. Technology vendors should be ready to evidence model risk, outsourcing and cyber controls, and South African regulators may follow.

items.title: Central Bank of Nigeria's regulations for non-security virtual assets entered into force
items.why: Nigeria now has a licensing route for virtual-asset operations.

items.title: Virtual Asset Service Providers Act transition ended: licensing, user ID and mixer bans now apply
items.why: Crypto providers in Kenya now need licences and KYC.

items.title: Online Safety Bill introduced (content moderation, age verification, new regulator)
items.why: Platforms and digital retailers operating in Kenya may face age checks and moderation duties.

items.title: Grace period ended for Egypt's Personal Data Protection Law (licences, cross-border transfers, security)
items.why: Full enforcement has started. Any organisation processing Egyptian customer or employee data needs a licence and a basis for cross-border transfers.

items.title: ICASA opened consultation on proposed Numbering Plan Fifth Amendment Regulations, 2026
items.why: Numbering changes affect operator systems and customer communications. Check the comment deadline.

items.title: Information Regulator fined First National Bank for failing to safeguard customer personal information
items.why: POPIA security-safeguard enforcement now comes with fines. Any organisation holding large customer datasets (loyalty, banking, e-commerce) should evidence access controls and breach handling.

items.title: FCCPC closed consultation on draft Sales Promotion (Amended) Regulations 2026
items.why: Promotions, competitions and loyalty campaigns in Nigeria may need approval under updated rules.

items.title: ICASA approved licence transfer from Itakane ICT to Zoom Fibre; Smile Telecoms transfer consultation closed
items.why: Fibre and wireless licences keep changing hands, which which can mean new owners and changing suppliers.

items.title: Competition Commission recommended unconditional approval of Teraco's acquisition of industrial land in Brackenfell (Cape Town)
items.why: More data-centre capacity is coming to Cape Town. That supports the case for in-country cloud hosting of workloads.

items.title: Minister issued Policy Direction on Electronic Communications Network Deployment
items.why: Sets the direction for rollout permissions and infrastructure sharing. Relevant to operators' fibre and tower build plans and to delivery timelines.

items.title: Amended Rule 39 of the Competition Commission Rules entered into force
items.why: A procedural change to Competition Commission rules that applies to everyone. Worth a quick check with legal teams on any filings or merger notifications in flight.

items.title: Bank of Ghana opened consultation on draft Credit Risk Management Directive 2026 (covers AI use)
items.why: Rules on AI in credit decisions are emerging in Ghana. Relevant to lending models and to vendors supplying them.

items.title: National Treasury closed consultation on draft National Payment System Bill 2026 (licensing, open finance, interoperability)
items.why: Open-finance and interoperability rules for payments could reshape checkout and wallet integrations in Kenya.

items.title: Communications Authority closed consultation on a licensing framework for data centres
items.why: Data centres in Kenya may soon need a licence, which affects regional hosting choices.

items.title: National Treasury and SARB closed consultation on draft crypto-assets manual for cross-border activities
items.why: Final cross-border crypto rules are next. Banks and payment providers will need updated exchange-control and reporting logic.

items.title: South Africa, Australia, Singapore, UAE and others adopted A Call for Control of Frontier AI Models
items.why: South Africa is aligning with frontier-AI safety commitments. Expect this to show up later in public-sector AI procurement criteria.

items.title: BRICS adopted New Delhi Declaration on AI governance, cybersecurity and online child safety
items.why: India and South Africa are both signatories, which is useful context for India–South Africa business and data-flow discussions.

items.title: Portfolio Committee closed consultation on Electronic Communications Amendment Bill 2026 (access obligations, competition authority governance)
items.why: The biggest telecoms law change in the pipeline. Access obligations and regulator powers could reshape wholesale pricing and network sharing.

items.title: Competition Commission approved Brink's acquisition of NCR Atleos (ATMs, cash services)
items.why: Consolidation in ATM and cash-services supply. A relevant input for store cash-handling and branch-network contracts.

items.title: Competition Commission recommended approval with conditions of Capitec's acquisition of Walletdoc
items.why: Payment-gateway consolidation, cleared with conditions. Retailers and banks should check gateway contracts and switching options.

items.title: South Africa among 29 signatories of the agreement establishing the World AI Cooperation Organization
items.why: Points to a more multipolar AI-governance stance, alongside the EU-style rules many organisations already track.

items.title: Competition Commission referred Audatex South Africa to the Tribunal over alleged price discrimination in vehicle-repair estimation software
items.why: Software pricing itself is now a competition target. This matters for insurers, and for any software vendor with tiered pricing in South Africa.
